articles.title: Crypto Trading Bot Backtesting: An Honest How-To Guide
articles.excerpt: Crypto trading bot backtesting means running a bot's rules over past market data to see how it would have traded, before you risk any money. Done honestly, it does not tell you whether a bot will make…
articles.body: Crypto trading bot backtesting means running a bot's rules over past market data to see how it would have traded, before you risk any money. Done honestly, it does not tell you whether a bot will make money. It tells you whether a bot is worth testing further, and most bots fail that test. This guide shows how to run a backtest that is hard to fool: realistic costs, enough trades, data the bot never saw, and a forward test on live prices. What crypto trading bot backtesting can and cannot tell you A backtest replays history.

articles.excerpt: At Ceptor Labs, we build software for problems we see up close. Today we're introducing Mocxam, a platform that lets coaching institutes launch their own branded online test series, without building s…
articles.body: At Ceptor Labs, we build software for problems we see up close. Today we're introducing Mocxam , a platform that lets coaching institutes launch their own branded online test series, without building software themselves. The problem we set out to solve Preparing for SSC, Banking, Railways or UPSC means taking a lot of mock tests. Behind most of those tests, a coaching institute is doing manual work: Questions live in documents and spreadsheets. Tests run on generic form tools with no real exam feel. There's often no negative marking, no section timers and no proper question palette. Students get a score, but no idea why they lost marks. The institute's own brand barely shows up. Large test-prep platforms cover parts of this, but the institute ends up promoting someone else's brand.

articles.title: Callback Function in JavaScript
articles.excerpt: A callback function is a function passed as an argument to another function so that it can be called later. function greet(name) { console.log("Hello " + name); } function user(callback) { callback("S…
articles.body: A callback function is a function passed as an argument to another function so that it can be called later. function greet ( name ) { console . log ( " Hello " + name ); } function user ( callback ) { callback ( " Sajin Joe " ); } user ( greet ); Output: Hello Sajin Joe Callback with a simple calculation function calculate ( a , b , callback ) { console . log ( callback ( a , b )); } function add ( x , y ) { return x + y ; } calculate ( 10 , 20 , add ); Output: 30 Callback with setTimeout() setTimeout ( function () { console . log ( " Hello JavaScript " ); }, 2000 ); Output: Hello JavaScript after approximately 2 seconds. The function passed to setTimeout() is a callback. The timer schedules it to run later.

articles.body: LibreChat: 12,283 fingerprints, 13,265 titles, and a chat front end that stores the keys to every model A chat application is a friendly interface over a credential store. LibreChat's deployment documentation asks the operator to supply provider keys for the models it will call, and those keys live in the application's configuration, which means the application is a secret store with a text box on it. The measurements On 23 October 2026, ZoomEye returned 12,283 matches for app="LibreChat" , 13,265 matches for title="LibreChat" , and 7,588 matches for title="LibreChat" && port="3080" . The fingerprint and title counts are within eight percent of each other, which is the pattern of a clean signature.

articles.body: Europe has dropped the ball on the prototype for its first reusable spacecraft. Or, rather, the prototype itself was dropped — on purpose — but the outcome of its fall was not what engineers had hoped for. The incident occurred during an Oct. 6 drop test of the full-scale Space Rider model , from the European Space Agency (ESA). The robotic vehicle's initial drogue parachute deployed successfully, but its main parafoil detached during deployment, leaving the prototype unable to slow its descent before crashing into the ground, according to ESA officials. The cause of the failure remains under investigation.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 22, 1992: Ashes of 'Star Trek' creator Gene Roddenberry launch into space on NASA shuttle
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of "Star Trek." Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of " Star Trek ," aboard. During mission STS-52, NASA astronaut and shuttle commander James Wetherbee brought a small container with a portion of Roddenberry's ashes into space as part of his personal effects at the request of Roddenberry's widow, Majel Barrett . It was Roddenberry's lifelong dream to go to space, but he never got to go while he was alive. But thanks to his wife, a little bit of Roddenberry finally made it to space almost exactly one year after his death. NASA and his family didn't tell anyone about it until almost two years later in 1994. Wetherbee said he was "honored to be asked" by Barrett to carry Roddenberry's ashses on the spaceflight.

articles.body: The total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027, has an ancient feel. However, its point of greatest eclipse occurs just a few miles from Thebes, the magnificent religious and political capital of ancient Egypt's Middle Kingdom and New Kingdom. On the east bank of the mighty Nile is Luxor, the great city of the living, with its massive temple complexes of Karnak and Luxor.
